correctness.rationale: The scalar quadratic Schur–Cohn conditions reduce exactly to q^2|a|^2<1 and F(q;a)>0. For |a|>1, F is nonpositive at both permitted q-endpoints, and the only alternative critical point q0=(1-Re a)/(|a|^2-Re a) has F(q0)=-((Im a)^2)(|a|^2-1)^2/(|a|^2-Re a)^2<=0. Consequently any stable weight forces q=1/3 to be a positive interior maximizer, with its own product bound. The |a|<=1 cases, matrix companion factorization, strict uniqueness on negative real a, and imaginary-axis cutoff are proved separately. The self-contained checker passed 97,272 numerical/rational tests; the analytic argument, not finite tests, establishes all quantifiers.

originality.rationale: Compared the full universal implication with published database entries and primary literature descriptions. Closest source arxiv:2609.21442v1 addresses equal-weight regions varying window length; this theorem instead fixes two memories and classifies all convex weights on complex spectra. value.rationale: The result fully classifies the inclusion-maximal stability domain for all constant convex two-memory weights and all finite complex matrices. The unique universal q=1/3 yields a sharp negative-real threshold -3 (versus -2 for the uniform q=1/2 scheme) and an exact pure-imaginary margin sqrt(6sqrt(3)-9); unlike a routine single-weight Schur test, this simultaneously dominates every admissible weight. This is a motivated numerical-design guarantee, not a claim of optimum per-instance rate or a paper-sized generalization.
